s2.p1: The Gambia has **no member** in the World DanceSport Federation. Its neighbour **Senegal** joined as a provisional member in 2022.
s2.p2: What exists: ==acrobatic rock’n’roll== at Flex Fuzion, a dance academy founded in 2017. In 2023, a Kololi hotel also ran **salsa Saturdays**.

s3.p: came to Janjanbureh’s historic island for the **9th Kankurang and Masks Festival**, 23–25 January 2026. Over **20 masquerades** performed.

s4.p1: In Dakar on **14 March 2026**, a Gambian couple won the A-Class title in **acrobatic rock’n’roll**, becoming the first African champions at that level.
s4.p2: Flex Fuzion’s team of 15 dancers came home with ==11 trophies==. Much of the trip was **self-funded**.

s5.name: KUMPO
s5.p: A whirl of **raffia palm** with a wooden stick fixed on top. The dancer spins on it, and is then seen as a **spirit**, not a person.

s5.name: ZIMBA
s5.p: Born from the tale of a hunter who calmed a **lion** with a song. Masked dancers with painted faces pick spectators to dance, and ==ask for dalasi== if unimpressed.

s6.p: Many Gambians say that if there are no **sabar drums** at an occasion, nobody will go. They play at family gatherings, religious meetings, rallies and markets.

s7.p: UNESCO lists the **Kankurang**, a Manding initiation rite shared with **Senegal**. Its masked figure, dressed in bark and leaves, does a staccato dance with **two machetes**.
s7.p2: The Kumpo went abroad: Gambia’s **Berending Kumpo Association** danced at Singapore’s ==Esplanade==, 1–3 May 2026.
